arbetsliv.title: Which decisions shape the future of working life?
arbetsliv.desc: Skills, new ways of working and the people behind the transition.
arbetsliv.body:
The future of working life rarely begins with a new technology. It begins with questions about who gets the opportunity to learn, who can gain a foothold and who has a say. As tasks change, employers and employees alike need to find ways to develop together.

Skills as part of everyday work|Learning needs a place even between major changes. A course can open a door, but it is in day-to-day work that new knowledge is put to the test. Time for mentoring, learning from colleagues and reflection are therefore concrete issues to raise with anyone discussing skills development.

Who is responsible?|Employers, education providers and society have different roles. The discussion becomes more useful when each participant describes their next step. Which skills are in demand? How can someone outside the labour market demonstrate their abilities? And how do we make development possible for those already in work?

Almedalen offers space to bring these perspectives together. A good discussion does not end with everyone agreeing. It clarifies what needs to be tried, by whom and on what terms.

energi.title: Green energy and Sweden’s next step
energi.desc: A transition that raises questions about technology, competitiveness and responsibility.
energi.body:
A conversation about energy can quickly become a debate about individual sources of power. But for a business, a household or a municipality, it is also about availability, costs and the ability to plan. The energy system of the future needs to be discussed as a whole.

From vision to location|Behind every investment is a place. This is where questions of land, infrastructure, the local environment and long-term development meet. Anyone seeking to understand the transition therefore needs to listen both to those building it and to those affected by the changes.

Several parts must work together|Generation, electricity grids, storage and consumption influence one another. Discussing just one part risks leaving crucial interdependencies out of the picture. A more concrete discussion begins with what the system needs to deliver and which obstacles stand in the way.

At an energy seminar, it is worth listening for responsibilities and timeframes. What can be done now? What requires collaboration over several years? When these questions receive clear answers, the path from ambition to action becomes easier to scrutinise.

vard.title: How tomorrow’s healthcare takes shape in practice
vard.desc: From digital tools to a clearer patient perspective.
vard.body:
People who need care do not encounter an organisational chart. They encounter a booking, a question, a treatment and sometimes a wait. That is why the discussion about the future of healthcare needs to begin with people’s journey through the system.

Technology with a clear purpose|A digital tool may be part of the solution, but the problem needs to be described first. Should the tool simplify contact, provide better information or free up time? Who will find things easier, and who might need another way to get help?

Room for experience|Patients, relatives and staff see different parts of healthcare. Their experiences need to come together when new ways of working are designed. It is not enough to ask whether a service works technically. It must also be understandable and usable in everyday life, where people have different circumstances and abilities.

In Almedalen’s healthcare discussions, major questions of reform can meet practical work. Listen for how proposals will be followed up: what change should patients notice, and how will staff be given the conditions they need to make it happen?

demokrati.title: Democracy begins when people meet
demokrati.desc: Room for different perspectives, difficult questions and new conversations.
demokrati.body:
Democratic conversations need room for both conviction and curiosity. Being able to say what you think is one part of the encounter. Being able to listen to someone who sees the issue differently is another.

Who gets to take part?|An open event does not automatically make a discussion accessible. Language, venue, timing and the way people are invited affect who can participate. The format matters too: can the audience ask questions, or does the discussion stay on stage?

Disagreement that can be understood|A constructive discussion does not have to end in agreement. Instead, it can clarify which values are in conflict, which facts need to be examined and what consequences different choices might have. The moderator’s task then becomes helping the audience understand the differences.

Almedalen can be a place where established voices meet new ones. For visitors, a good starting point is to choose something familiar and something that challenges their own view. The question to take along is simple: which perspective is missing from this room?

hallbarhet.title: Sustainability that makes a difference after the stage lights go out
hallbarhet.desc: From big ambitions to choices whose results can be tracked.
hallbarhet.body:
Sustainability is a word that encompasses many ambitions. For the discussion to be useful, it also needs a defined scope. Which impacts do we want to change, what can we control and how will we know whether the work is moving in the right direction?

Make the issue concrete|For an organiser, it might be about travel, materials or food. For another organisation, the focus may lie elsewhere. The first step is to describe your own situation and choose measures on that basis, rather than starting with the most visible symbol.

Show the trade-offs too|Not every decision is straightforward. Accessibility, finances and environmental considerations may need to be weighed against one another. Credibility is strengthened when that balancing act can be understood. Which alternatives were considered? Why was a particular path chosen? What remains to be resolved?

A discussion about sustainability becomes especially interesting when the next step can be put into words. Take a question from the stage back to your own organisation: what could we change, follow up and report on openly when we meet next time?

digitalisering.title: AI in everyday life – what questions do we need to ask?
digitalisering.desc: People, responsibility and judgement as new tools become part of our lives.
digitalisering.body:
When AI is discussed, the focus often falls on what the technology can do. An equally important question is what we want to use it for. A tool needs a clear context, a defined need and someone who takes responsibility for the result.

Start with the task|Which step should become easier? What requires human judgement? And which errors would matter? These questions help an organisation choose a sensible first application and understand when the technology is not suitable.

Trust requires transparency|Anyone using AI support needs to understand its limitations. Anyone affected by a decision needs to be able to find out how it was reached and where to direct their questions. Technology choices and the allocation of responsibility therefore need to be discussed together.

Almedalen offers an opportunity to bring together developers, users and people affected by new systems. A good discussion goes beyond opportunities and concerns. It shows how an application will be tested, scrutinised and improved.

naringsliv.title: What do businesses need to dare to take the next step?
naringsliv.desc: Investments take shape where ideas meet the conditions of everyday life.
naringsliv.body:
An idea does not become an investment by itself. Between ambition and implementation lie questions about people, financing, infrastructure and demand. The conditions businesses face become clearer when the discussion starts with a concrete next step.

Different businesses, different obstacles|A small service company and an industrial operation may face very different challenges. It is therefore useful to ask who a proposal actually helps and how. This also makes the discussion about competitiveness more precise.

Cooperation needs a task|When business, education and the public sector come together, there are opportunities to resolve shared issues. But cooperation needs a purpose. Is the task to find skills, test an idea or simplify a process? Who can make decisions, and who needs to take part?

For anyone attending a business seminar, a useful listening tip is to distinguish between general wishes and concrete commitments. The latter show what can actually happen after the participants have left the stage.

utbildning.title: Learning that stays with us throughout life
utbildning.desc: How do we make room for new knowledge at different stages of life?
utbildning.body:
Learning does not belong only to a particular age or place. People need to be able to develop their knowledge when working life changes, when interests grow and when life takes a new direction. But the opportunity to study looks different for different people.

Accessibility is more than a place on a course|Time, finances, prior knowledge and life circumstances affect whether education can be completed. Flexible education therefore needs to be assessed from the perspective of the person who will use it. What does it take to begin, continue and finish?

Knowledge needs to meet real needs|The needs of working life are an important part of the discussion, but education also has broader purposes. The ability to think critically, understand other perspectives and participate in society needs room alongside more specific skills requirements.

These perspectives can meet in Almedalen’s discussions about education. Ask how a proposal affects both today’s participants and those who have not yet found a way in. An educational opportunity only becomes real when people can take it.

sakerhet.title: A safer society is also built in everyday life
sakerhet.desc: Preparedness, cooperation and the ability to keep essential functions running.
sakerhet.body:
Safety and preparedness are major societal issues, but they often take shape in everyday decisions. Who knows what to do if something stops working? How does information reach people? Which services need to keep operating even under difficult conditions?

Understand the interdependencies|An organisation may depend on electricity, transport, digital services and other organisations. Describing these connections is one way to make vulnerabilities understandable. It also provides a basis for deciding what needs to be strengthened first.

Plans need users|A plan gains value when people know about it and have the opportunity to act. Responsibilities, channels of contact and expectations need to be clear. Exercises and shared reflection can reveal questions that are otherwise easy to miss on paper.

In Almedalen, the discussion about security can bring together the societal perspective and organisations’ experiences. A useful question to take to a seminar is what different stakeholders need from one another for cooperation to work when circumstances change.

manskliga-rattigheter.title: Whose perspectives have a place when society changes?
manskliga-rattigheter.desc: Human rights as a starting point for concrete societal issues.
manskliga-rattigheter.body:
When society changes, people are affected in different ways. A decision that makes things easier for one group may create new barriers for another. A rights-based perspective helps us ask questions about participation, how people are treated and who actually gains access to an opportunity.

Listen before the solution is finalised|People affected by a change need the opportunity to contribute their experiences. This requires more than an invitation. The format of participation, the language and the ability to influence the outcome need to be carefully considered.

From principle to practice|Broad principles need to be connected to concrete situations. How does a service work for different users? Which voices are included in the information used to make decisions? How can someone who encounters a barrier make their voice heard? Questions like these make it possible to follow up on the discussion.

Almedalen can create encounters between people who do not otherwise share the same room. Its value also lies in what participants take away. A new perspective can be the beginning of a better question, a changed way of working or a partnership that continues after the week.

amne-34-1.desc: Older people have different experiences, wishes and circumstances.
amne-34-1.body:
Older people have different experiences, wishes and circumstances.

From the topic to everyday life|Discussions about ageing need to make room for both self-determination and effective support. Those affected need to be able to contribute their own view of what matters.

A question to take into the discussion|How do we avoid treating a group as though everyone’s needs were the same? A concrete starting point is to ask for examples of situations in which a choice makes a difference. This makes it easier to understand both the ambition and what needs to be resolved during implementation.

Further in the programme|This sample article is linked to the event “From neglected to prioritised – is a national eye health strategy crucial to eye health in Sweden?”. Read the programme description and use the discussion as an introduction to the topic. The article is an illustrative text and does not reproduce the organiser’s statements or positions.
